newsitem.title: UK: Bock still interested in Lonrho trading arm.
newsitem.headline: Bock still interested in Lonrho trading arm.

text.p: Former Lonrho boss Dieter Bock, who earlier agreed a property partnership with Canada's TrizecHahn Corp, said on Wednesday he might still become a shareholder in Lonrho's African trading operations once they were spun off.
But Bock said the deal with TrizecHahn would not allow him to take up any post to help manage the trading business, which Lonrho seeks to demerge.
"If there is anything coming up in the near future, I would maybe be interested in a form of an investment, but not in terms of management at all," Bock told journalists.
The German businessman said he would retire as Lonrho's deputy chairman after he formed a strategic alliance with TrizecHahn to expand the Canadian firm's European real estate presence.
Bock became Lonrho's deputy chairman late in 1997 when he gave up his job as chief executive to prevent conflict of interest as the British conglomerate was splitting itself up.
At the same time as stepping down as chief executive, Bock sold his 18.3 percent stake in Lonrho to South Africa's Anglo American Corp.
Asked whether he planned to re-invest all the proceeds in a separate African trading company, he said: "I cannot predict that because I do not know any conditions yet."

Bock said he no longer owned any Lonrho shares. He added there was no deal with Anglo which would give him the option to buy the South African company's stake in Lonrho's trading business once it had been demerged.
"There is no agreement in place with Lonrho in that respect," he said.
